toolchain.install: Install Visual Studio Build Tools (Windows), gcc or clang (Linux) or the Xcode Command Line Tools (macOS)

backends.safety: clangd runs in a mirror of the repository with a compile database in {outside}/cdb: an existing compile_commands.json (paths rewritten to the mirror), one CMake (FETCHCONTENT_FULLY_DISCONNECTED, VCPKG_MANIFEST_INSTALL=OFF, CPM_USE_LOCAL_PACKAGES) or Meson (--wrap-mode=nodownload) configures into {outside}/cbuild/<compiler> after trace index --allow-build (configure runs the project's build scripts; nothing is built), or, without a build system, a database trace writes from syntax facts (-x c / -x c++, include directories). --query-driver names only the detected compilers; the background index is persisted in {outside}/cdb/.cache (never in the repository) and waited for after the first documents open, bounded: its end, a stall (no end and no shard change for 120 s: queries use the index as it is) or ready_timeout_secs (server_timeout); no .clangd/user config, no clang-tidy, no header insertion, preambles in memory. Sources a real build's database does not list are outside the build (not asked); inactive #if regions are reported by clangd and their calls are inactive_code. Linux / Windows on aarch64 have no clangd release: a clangd installed with the system (PATH, /usr/bin/clangd-NN, LLVM) is used, else the server is unavailable (servers/c_cpp.rs).
